claim: Dave’s rewrite: M-CAM work is finished, so emphasise the orbital phase and the science instruments.
note: accept suggestion but remove the grant information.

suggestion.to: OU academics were members of BepiColombo's M-CAM monitoring camera team, analysing images returned during the spacecraft's Mercury flybys, and have led ESA's Mercury Surface and Composition Working Group. The Open University was also a development partner, alongside instrument lead the University of Leicester, in building the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer (MIXS). OU scientists are now Co-Investigators on MIXS and on MERTIS (the Mercury Thermal Infrared Spectrometer), associates on SIMBIO-SYS (the orbiter's spectrometer and imaging system), and hold a share of a £3 million STFC 'Astronomy Large Award' to do science from Mercury orbit.
